# QS-CFW-9335-36 - Quality specification - gear blank CFW-9335-36 (8620)

Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P3  
Parts: CFW-9335-36

Scope

This quality specification establishes acceptance criteria, inspection methods, and nonconformance handling for gear blank CFW-9335-36 (CFW-9335-36) manufactured of 8620 material at Plant P3. It applies to finished forging blanks delivered to machining and heat treatment operations. The intent is to ensure dimensional accuracy and material condition sufficient for downstream transformation into final gears while minimizing rework and scrap.

Requirements table

- Part identification
  - Part: CFW-9335-36 (CFW-9335-36)
  - Material: 8620

- Hardness
  - The hardness range for gear blank CFW-9335-36 (CFW-9335-36) is 36-41 HRC.

- Bore
  - Bore diameter tolerance for gear blank CFW-9335-36 (CFW-9335-36) is ±0.09 mm.

- Weight
  - The maximum forging weight for gear blank CFW-9335-36 (CFW-9335-36) is 107.9 kg.

- Surface condition
  - Forging surfaces shall be free of forging laps, cold shuts, and open defects that would impair safe machining to final geometry. Surface blemishes that can be removed by normal clean-up passes are acceptable.

- Identification and traceability
  - Each lot shall be accompanied by a material test report and a forging traveler that links heat lot to individual blanks. The traveler shall reference this document id QS-CFW-9335-36.

Inspection method

General approach
Inspections shall be performed by trained quality personnel following documented procedures in the plant quality system. The objective is to verify that forgings meet the requirements table. Inspectors shall record findings on the forging traveler and retain records as described in Records to keep.

Hardness verification
Surface hardness checks shall be taken at representative locations on the blank where machining will not remove the test area. Measurements shall be taken on the forged surface after any planned stress relief but prior to final machining. The measured hardness shall fall within the specified range. The hardness range for gear blank CFW-9335-36 (CFW-9335-36) is 36-41 HRC. When portable hardness testers are used, calibration of the instrument shall be verified against certified blocks prior to use.

Bore measurement
Bore diameters shall be measured using plug gauges or calibrated bore gauges appropriate for the nominal bore geometry. The bore diameter tolerance for gear blank CFW-9335-36 (CFW-9335-36) is ±0.09 mm. When using gauging methods that produce a go/no-go decision, the go/no-go limits shall be set to the nominal bore plus and minus the tolerance. When using direct-reading instruments, recorded values shall be entered on the traveler and compared to tolerance limits.

Weight check
Each forging shall be weighed on a calibrated scale capable of the expected mass range. The maximum forging weight for gear blank CFW-9335-36 (CFW-9335-36) is 107.9 kg. Any blank that exceeds this weight shall be held for engineering disposition to evaluate material distribution, potential flash, or excess stock that could affect downstream processes.

Visual and surface inspections
Conduct a systematic visual inspection under adequate lighting. Look for laps, cracks, cracks circumferentially, and other discontinuities. Minor surface irregularities that are fully machined away are acceptable if they do not compromise part integrity or material traceability. Document any anomalies on the traveler with photographs where helpful.

Sampling and lot acceptance
Sampling shall be based on process capability and risk; inspect representative pieces from each furnace lot and die set combination. When an out-of-tolerance condition is found within a lot, escalate to 100 percent inspection of the lot until root cause and corrective actions are implemented.

Records to keep
- Completed forging traveler with inspector signature and dates of inspections.
- Hardness test records including instrument identification and calibration reference.
- Bore measurement records with instrument identification and calibration reference.
- Scale weight records showing the measured weight for each blank or lot summary.
- Photographic records for any nonconforming surface conditions.
All records shall be retained in accordance with plant document retention policy and shall be made available for customer or internal audits upon request. The traveler shall reference this document id QS-CFW-9335-36 to maintain traceability.

Nonconformance handling

Identification and segregation
Any forging that fails to meet the requirements table shall be tagged and segregated from conforming material immediately. The tag shall reference the specific failing characteristic and the forging traveler.

Containment and notification
Quality shall notify manufacturing supervision and engineering when a nonconformance is discovered. A containment action shall be initiated to prevent further shipment or use of affected forgings.

Disposition
Disposition options include rework, repair, or scrap. Examples of allowed dispositions:
- Minor surface blemishes that can be removed by standard clean-up machining passes may be approved for machining after engineering review.
- Forgings exceeding the maximum mass shall be evaluated for removal of excess flash or machining allowance; if removal is not feasible or would compromise part integrity, scrap shall be issued.
All dispositions that constitute a deviation from this specification require engineering documentation and approval. The disposition record shall be attached to the forging traveler.

Root cause and corrective action
For any lot with a confirmed nonconformance, perform root cause analysis and implement corrective actions. Document findings, actions taken, and verification steps on the corrective action record linked to the traveler.

Audit and continuous improvement
Quality shall review inspection results periodically to identify trends. Process improvements and tooling adjustments shall be prioritized when recurring issues are identified. Continuous improvement actions and their verification shall be documented and retained with related records.

Related documents
None cited.

Revision history
Rev E entered to reflect current requirements for Plant P3 and parts CFW-9335-36.
